topics: 🙏 Prolonging Prayer, Table, and Bathroom — when 'lengthening' is a virtue and when it is a fault
🍞 The Table That Atones — Ezekiel's altar-turned-table and the three things that shorten life
👑 Three Things That Need Mercy — a good king, a good year, a good dream
🛠️ Bezalel — consulting the community, the order of Tabernacle-then-vessels, and the letters of Creation
💭 Rav Ḥisda on Dreams — a dream not interpreted is like a letter not read
🗣️ Bettering a Dream — the formula before three, the prayer during Birkat Kohanim, and 'all dreams follow the mouth'

overview.title: 📖 Overview: From Long Prayers to the Science of Dreams
overview.subtitle: Berakhot 55a–55b
overview.hebrewSource: חֶלְמָא דְּלָא מְפַשַּׁר כְּאִגַּרְתָּא דְּלָא מִקַּרְיָא
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: The daf opens by reconciling praise for one who prolongs his prayer, his meal, and his time in the bathroom with sources that condemn each. A series of 'threes' follows: three things that shorten life, three that need mercy, three that God proclaims Himself. The appointment of Bezalel teaches that a leader needs the community's consent and that his name reflects his wisdom. Then the Gemara turns to dreams: Rav Ḥisda's maxims, Joseph's dream that was only partly fulfilled, the formula for 'bettering' a troubling dream before three people, the prayer said during the Priestly Blessing, and the principle that all dreams follow the mouth of the interpreter.

slides.title: 🙏 Three Things Rav Yehuda Praised Prolonging
slides.subtitle: Each praise seems contradicted by another source; each is resolved by a distinction

boxes.title: Prayer
items: Objection: 'Hope deferred makes the heart sick' (Proverbs 13:12); Rabbi Yitzḥak lists expecting prayer to be answered among three things that recall one's sins
Resolution: bad when one expects to be answered (מְעַיֵּין בַּהּ); good when one simply increases supplication

boxes.title: The Table
items: Why is it good? Perhaps a poor person will come and the host can feed him at once
Ezekiel 41:22 begins 'the altar' and ends 'the table before the Lord'
Rabbi Yoḥanan and Rabbi Elazar: while the Temple stood the altar atoned; now a person's table atones for him

boxes.title: The Bathroom
items: Objection: a baraita lists ten causes of hemorrhoids, and some say 'one who suspends himself too much in the bathroom'
Resolution: harmful when he prolongs and suspends himself; healthy when he prolongs without suspending
Rabbi Yehuda son of Rabbi Ilai told the matron his healthy face came from examining himself in the 24 bathrooms between his lodging and the study hall

callout.label: Method:
callout.text: The Gemara does not reject either source; it splits the case. The same act is a virtue in one form and a fault in another.

slides.title: 🔢 The Daf's Lists of Three
slides.subtitle: Rav Yehuda, Rav, and Rabbi Yoḥanan each teach a triad with a verse for every item
rows: Rav Yehuda: shorten a person's days
Given a Torah scroll and not reading; given a cup of blessing and not blessing; conducting oneself with an air of superiority (רַבָּנוּת)
'It is your life and the length of your days' (Deut. 30:20); 'I will bless them that bless you' (Gen. 12:3); Joseph died before his brothers (Ex. 1:6) because he acted with superiority
Rav Yehuda in Rav's name: require mercy
A good king, a good year, a good dream
'The king's heart is in the hand of the Lord' (Prov. 21:1); 'the eyes of the Lord are always upon it' (Deut. 11:12); 'You will recover me [וְתַחֲלִימֵנִי]' (Isaiah 38:16) read as ḥalom
'The Lord has called for a famine' (II Kings 8:1); 'I will call for the grain' (Ezek. 36:29); 'I have called by name Bezalel' (Ex. 31:1–2)
A morning dream; a dream one's fellow dreamed about him; a dream interpreted within a dream
Some add a repeated dream: 'the dream was doubled unto Pharaoh' (Gen. 41:32)

callout.label: Bridge:
callout.text: The verse about Bezalel launches the next discussion of his appointment, and 'a good dream' launches the long treatment of dreams.

slides.title: 🛠️ Bezalel: Appointed by Consent, Named for Wisdom
slides.subtitle: Rabbi Yitzḥak and Rabbi Yonatan read Exodus 35:30 and the order of the Tabernacle's construction

lines.speaker: R' Yitzḥak
lines.text: One may appoint a leader over a community only after consulting the community: 'See, the Lord has called by name Bezalel' (Exodus 35:30).

lines.speaker: God to Moses
lines.text: Moses, is Bezalel suitable in your eyes? — Master of the universe, if he is suitable before You, all the more so before me! — Nevertheless, go and tell them.

lines.speaker: Israel
lines.text: If he is suitable before the Holy One and before you, all the more so before us!

lines.speaker: R' Yonatan
lines.text: Bezalel was named for his wisdom. God told Moses: make a Tabernacle, ark, and vessels. Moses reversed it: ark, vessels, and Tabernacle.

lines.speaker: Bezalel
lines.text: Moses our teacher, the way of the world is to build a house and then bring in the vessels. If I make the vessels first, where shall I put them? Perhaps God said: Tabernacle, ark, and vessels?

lines.speaker: Moses
lines.text: Perhaps you were in God's shadow (בְּצֵל אֵל) and knew! Rav adds: Bezalel knew how to join the letters with which heaven and earth were created — wisdom, understanding, knowledge (Ex. 31:3; Prov. 3:19–20).

callout.label: Rabbi Yoḥanan:
callout.text: God grants wisdom only to one who already has wisdom: 'He gives wisdom unto the wise' (Daniel 2:21). Rabbi Abbahu derived the same from 'in the hearts of all who are wise-hearted I have placed wisdom' (Exodus 31:6).

slides.title: 💭 Rav Ḥisda's Rules of Dreaming
slides.subtitle: A string of maxims that set the daf's theory of dreams

steps.content: 1️⃣ Any dream — but not one during a fast
2️⃣ חֶלְמָא דְּלָא מְפַשַּׁר כְּאִגַּרְתָּא דְּלָא מִקַּרְיָא — a dream not interpreted is like a letter not read
3️⃣ Neither a good dream nor a bad dream is entirely fulfilled — Rabbi Berekhya proves it from Joseph: the moon bowed, yet his mother was already dead (Gen. 37:9)
4️⃣ A bad dream is better than a good one (it brings remorse); its sadness suffices, just as a good dream's joy suffices. Rav Yosef: even for me, the joy of a good dream negates it
5️⃣ A bad dream is worse than lashes: 'God has so made it that men should fear before Him' (Eccl. 3:14) — Rabbi Yoḥanan: that is a bad dream

6️⃣ Rabbi Shimon bar Yoḥai: as grain cannot grow without straw, no dream is without idle matter (Jeremiah 23:28); Rabbi Levi: expect a good dream's fulfillment up to 22 years, Joseph's span from age 17 to the end of the famine

callout.label: Rav Huna:
callout.text: A good person is not shown a good dream and a wicked person is not shown a bad dream. David never saw a good dream; Ahitophel never saw a bad one. Since Psalms 91:10 promises the righteous will not be frightened by bad dreams, the Gemara concludes David saw dreams but did not understand what he saw — and Rabbi Zeira says one who sleeps seven days without a dream is called 'evil'.

slides.title: 🗣️ What To Do With a Troubling Dream
slides.subtitle: Rabbi Yoḥanan's remedy before three, the prayer at Birkat Kohanim, and why the interpreter's mouth matters

nodes.content: ❓ Rabbi Yoḥanan: one distraught by a dream should 'interpret it' before three. But Rav Ḥisda said an uninterpreted dream is an unread letter — why promote its fulfillment?

💡 Read instead: he should better it (יְטִיבֶנּוּ) before three. He says 'I saw a good dream'; they answer 'it is good and let it be good, may the Merciful One make it good; seven times may Heaven decree that it be good'
📜 They recite three 'transformations' (Ps. 30:12, Jer. 31:12, Deut. 23:6), three 'redemptions' (Ps. 55:19, Isa. 35:10, I Sam. 14:45), and three 'peaces' (Isa. 57:19, I Chr. 12:19, I Sam. 25:6)

columns.label: Don't know what you saw?
columns.content: Ameimar, Mar Zutra and Rav Ashi: stand before the priests as they lift their hands and say 'Master of the Universe, I am Yours and my dreams are Yours…' finishing as the congregation answers amen

columns.label: Shmuel's practice
columns.content: After a bad dream: 'the dreams speak falsely' (Zech. 10:2); after a good one: 'I speak with him in a dream' (Num. 12:6). Rava: the first is by a demon, the second by an angel

nodes.content: ✅ Rabbi Bena'a went to 24 interpreters in Jerusalem; each gave a different reading and all came true — כׇּל הַחֲלוֹמוֹת הוֹלְכִים אַחַר הַפֶּה, all dreams follow the mouth (Gen. 41:13). Rava: only when the interpretation fits the dream (Gen. 41:12)

callout.label: Rabbi Yonatan:
callout.text: A person is shown only the thoughts of his own heart (Daniel 2:29–30). Rava: that is why no one dreams of a golden palm tree or an elephant passing through the eye of a needle.

summary.principle: Whether it is a prolonged prayer or a night's dream, meaning depends on how one holds it: expectation ruins prayer, and interpretation shapes a dream, because all dreams follow the mouth.

flowSteps.content: 🙏 Prolonging prayer, table, bathroom — praised by Rav Yehuda, each qualified: no expectation, feeding the poor, no straining
🔢 Lists of three: what shortens life; what needs mercy (king, year, dream); what God proclaims (famine, plenty, leader)
🛠️ Bezalel: appointed only with the community's consent; named for wisdom; knew the letters of Creation

columns.content: 💭 Rav Ḥisda: an uninterpreted dream is an unread letter; no dream is wholly fulfilled; no dream lacks idle matter
🗣️ A troubling dream is 'bettered' before three, or handed to God during the Priestly Blessing

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: כׇּל הַחֲלוֹמוֹת הוֹלְכִים אַחַר הַפֶּה — all dreams follow the mouth of the interpreter, provided the interpretation fits the dream

quiz.q: How does the Gemara reconcile Rav Yehuda's praise for prolonging prayer with the teaching that prolonging prayer leads to heartache?
o: Prolonging is good only in the morning prayer
Prolonging is bad when one expects the prayer to be answered, and good when one merely increases supplication
Prolonging is good only for a Torah scholar
Prolonging is bad only on a fast day
quiz.e: The Gemara distinguishes between one who is 'me'ayen bah' — expects his prayer to be accepted — which leads to heartache, and one who simply adds supplication without such expectation.

quiz.q: According to Rabbi Yoḥanan and Rabbi Elazar, what does a person's table accomplish now that the Temple is destroyed?
o: It substitutes for the Shabbat candles
It atones for him, as the altar once atoned for Israel
It obligates him to invite a Torah scholar
It replaces the cup of blessing
quiz.e: Ezekiel 41:22 begins with 'the altar' and ends with 'the table'; while the Temple stood the altar atoned, and now one's table atones — for example by feeding the poor who come during a meal.

quiz.q: What does Rabbi Yitzḥak derive from God asking Moses whether Bezalel was suitable in his eyes?
o: That a leader must be from the tribe of Judah
That a leader may be appointed over a community only if the community is consulted
That Moses had authority to veto divine appointments
That craftsmen require rabbinic ordination
quiz.e: God asked Moses, and then had Moses ask Israel, whether Bezalel was suitable — teaching that a communal leader is appointed only with the community's consent.

quiz.q: Why does the Gemara reread Rabbi Yoḥanan's instruction that a distraught dreamer should 'interpret' his dream before three people?
o: Because three people cannot agree on an interpretation
Because interpreting a dream promotes its fulfillment, per Rav Ḥisda's 'unread letter' maxim, so he should instead 'better' it
Because only a professional interpreter may be consulted
Because the dream must first be reported to the priests
quiz.e: Since an uninterpreted dream is like an unread letter that cannot be fulfilled, one worried about a dream should not have it interpreted; rather, he should have three people declare it good and recite verses of transformation, redemption, and peace.

quiz.q: What caveat does Rava attach to the principle that 'all dreams follow the mouth' of the interpreter?
o: The interpreter must be paid
The interpretation must be given within three days
The interpretation must be akin to the dream, as Joseph interpreted 'each man according to his dream'
The interpreter must be one of the twenty-four in Jerusalem
quiz.e: Rava limits the principle to an interpretation that fits the dream's content, citing Genesis 41:12, 'each man according to his dream he did interpret'.
